title: Kafka DLT never engages: poison records and handler failures are silently dropped
actual: BaseKafkaConsumer.decodeContained() returns null on any decode failure and the listener ack-skips. KafkaProperties.Retry is documented 'INTENTIONALLY UNUSED'. BaseKafkaListenerConfig installs DefaultErrorHandler + DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer, but no listener path throws, so retry and DLT routing never fire.
expected: Malformed or poison records route to a DLQ with operator visibility; transient handler failures are retried before the offset advances.
trigger: Any unparseable payload, or any exception thrown inside a @KafkaListener handler body.
root_cause: Ack-always poison posture combined with a dead retry/DLT configuration block.
consequences: Silent loss of order/payment/shipping/rating/media events; no DLQ, no replay path, no alerting. Offset advances as if the event had been handled.
remediation: Let handler failures propagate to the container error handler (or publish explicitly to a DLQ), and either wire or delete the dead Retry block.
regression_test: Unit test: a consumer given a malformed payload must publish to the DLT topic; the offset must not advance as a silent success.

title: Four published lifecycle topics have no consumer: inventory, promotion, category, brand
actual: Producers publish shop.inventory.events.v1, shop.promotion.lifecycle.v1, shop.category.lifecycle.v1 and shop.brand.lifecycle.v1. A fleet-wide scan for @KafkaListener shows no consumer bound to any of these four topics.
expected: Every published lifecycle topic either has a consumer or is explicitly documented as fire-and-forget audit.
root_cause: Topics declared by producers without a matching consumer contract.
consequences: Published events accumulate with no consumer; documentation implies downstream projections that do not exist.
remediation: Document the four topics as unconsumed, or implement the missing projections (for example category/brand into the search index).
regression_test: Static topology test: every produced topic must have a declared consumer or an explicit allow-list entry.

title: Dead legacy topic-name configuration in KafkaProperties.Topics
actual: shop.kafka.topics.* defaults to order-events / payment-events / notification-events / inventory-events. No service references these keys; the real topic names are shop.*.lifecycle.v1 string literals in the publishers.
expected: Configuration properties map to values actually consumed, or are removed.
trigger: An operator reading configuration to discover topic names.
root_cause: Pre-v1 naming retained after the topic rename.
consequences: Misleading configuration; an operator could 'fix' a key that nothing reads.
remediation: Remove the Topics block or bind it to the real topic names.
regression_test: Config-binding test asserting shop.kafka.topics values equal the literals used by the publishers.

title: OAuth2 ROPC grant used for end-user login and for the Keycloak master-realm admin token
actual: KeycloakTokenClient.login() posts grant_type=password with the end user's username and password. KeycloakAdminClient.getAdminAccessToken() posts grant_type=password to the master realm with admin-cli plus admin username/password.
expected: Authorization Code + PKCE for user auth; client_credentials (or a service-account token) for the admin path. ROPC is deprecated by the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP.
trigger: Every user login and every admin operation.
root_cause: Password grant chosen for first-party login convenience.
consequences: Users disclose their password to the client; no MFA binding; the master-realm admin credential flows through a plain password grant on every admin call.
remediation: Assess migration to Authorization Code + PKCE and to a service-account client for admin operations. Retain ROPC only with a documented client-compatibility decision.
regression_test: Contract test against Keycloak asserting the grant type per flow; negative test that a client with ROPC disabled fails closed.

title: JWT audience validation is implemented but never configured - a token for any client in the realm is accepted by every service
actual: BaseSecurityConfig adds a JwtClaimValidator for 'aud' only when shop.security.expected-audiences is non-empty. A grep for 'expected-audiences' across every application.yml returns no match, so the installed validator chain is issuer + timestamp only in every deployment.
expected: Each resource server validates that the token audience contains the client id it serves.
trigger: Any request carrying a realm token minted for a different client.
root_cause: A security control implemented behind a default-empty property that no service sets.
consequences: Horizontal privilege escalation: a token issued to a low-privilege client is honoured by a high-privilege service.
remediation: Set shop.security.expected-audiences per service (and platform-wide) so the aud validator is actually installed.
regression_test: Integration test: a JWT with aud=[other-client] must be rejected with 401 by each service's decoder.

title: Shared default config ships default Keycloak master-realm admin credentials and a wildcard CORS origin
actual: shop.keycloak.admin-username and admin-password default to admin/admin; CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS defaults to '*' in .env.example line 157; docker-compose.yml requires KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD but .env.example ships 'admin'.
expected: No credential default inside a shared library; wildcard origins are never the shipped default.
trigger: A deployment that starts the platform without overriding the environment variables.
root_cause: Developer-friendly defaults retained in a library that production consumes.
consequences: Master-realm admin takeover if the default password survives into a real environment; any-origin reads on unauthenticated endpoints.
remediation: Remove credential defaults (fail fast when unset) and make the CORS default an explicit localhost list.
regression_test: Config test asserting the shared application.yml contains no resolvable credential default.

title: Contradictory bean-validation constraints on SecurityProperties.Cors.maxAgeSeconds
actual: The property carries both @Min(0) and @Positive; @Positive implies > 0 so @Min(0) is dead.
root_cause: Overlapping annotations left from an edit.
consequences: maxAgeSeconds=0 is rejected although @Min(0) implies it should be allowed.
remediation: Remove @Min(0) or @Positive, keeping the intended rule.
regression_test: Validation test binding maxAgeSeconds=0 and asserting the documented behaviour.

title: Object-storage access/secret key default to rustfsadmin in the shared library
actual: StorageProperties defaults accessKey and secretKey to 'rustfsadmin'.
expected: No credential defaults; fail fast when unset.
trigger: A service that enables shop.storage without overriding the credentials.
consequences: A deployment could point at a real bucket using the default RustFS admin credential.
remediation: Default to blank and validate at startup when storage is enabled.
regression_test: Configuration test asserting blank-by-default credentials and a startup failure when enabled without credentials.

title: server.error.include-message=always exposes internal exception text to API clients
actual: Shared defaults set server.error.include-message: always and include-binding-errors: always with include-stacktrace: never.
expected: Generic error text for 5xx; detailed text only for 4xx client errors.
trigger: Any unhandled server-side exception (SQL, I/O, SDK) in a service that does not override the block.
root_cause: Shared default tuned for developer ergonomics.
consequences: Internal messages (SQL fragments, hostnames, stack-derived detail) can reach end users.
remediation: Default include-message to never and let the platform exception handler emit the curated ApiResponse message instead.
regression_test: WebMvc test asserting a 500 response body contains no internal exception text.
